entities.summary: Johann Konrad Wilhelm Löhe was a pastor of the Lutheran Church, Confesional Lutheran writer, and is often regarded as being a founder of the deaconess movement in Lutheranism and a founding sponsor of the Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod (LCMS). From the small town of Neuendettelsau, he sent pastors to North America, Australia, New Guinea, Brazil, and Ukraine. His work for a clear confessional basis within the Bavarian church sometimes led to conflict with the ecclesiastical bureaucracy. His chief concern was that a parish find its life in the eucharist, and from that source evangelism and social ministries would flow.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Löhe's work in establishing a clear confessional basis within the Bavarian church led to the creation of the Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod (LCMS), which has had a significant impact on Lutheranism and American Protestantism. His efforts also influenced the development of the deaconess movement in Lutheranism.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Löhe's work in establishing a clear confessional basis led to the establishment of the Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod (LCMS), which has had a significant impact on Lutheranism in North America. His efforts also contributed to the spread of Christianity to new regions, including Australia and New Guinea.
